description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of a Gram stain preparation. Numerous gram-positive cocci, appearing as round, purple-stained organisms, are visible. They are arranged predominantly in clusters, a characteristic feature of certain bacterial species. The background is clear, with no visible host cells or debris.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing yeast-like organisms with surrounding inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows clusters of round to oval yeast-like organisms, some of which appear to be budding. The organisms are stained red, suggesting the use of a fungal-specific stain such as PAS (Periodic Acid-Schiff) or GMS (Gomori Methenamine Silver). Surrounding the organisms, there is evidence of inflammatory cells, likely neutrophils, indicating an ongoing immune response. The background appears to be connective tissue.
